title: Memory policing: abridged-context degradation + hedged retries for OOM resilience
creator: Marisol Chen
description: Implement an experiment-grade memory policing mechanism that gracefully reduces per-request working set (abridged context + selective KV omission) and issues hedged retries to fallback model variants when GPU allocation would otherwise trigger OOM. Goal is to improve p99 tail OOM rate under mixed-length workloads without large latency regressions.
acceptance_criteria: p99 OOM rate for noisy-mixed workloads reduced by >= 70% on the staging fleet compared to baseline (no policing) with < 15% median latency increase
Automated end-to-end test that injects memory pressure reproduces abridged-context path and triggers hedged retries deterministically
Telemetry dashboards show correct labels for degraded requests (policy.reason=abridged_context or policy.reason=kv_omit) and downstream failures are < 1% after retry
Feature gated behind runtime flag and rollbackable via config; rollout documented in runbook
design_decision_log: 2026-03-02: Chose abridged-context approach (trim oldest user turns + summary-preserving compression) instead of dropping model layers to keep output semantics intact
2026-03-03: KV omission policy will be per-request and prioritized by token-age/score; avoid global eviction to preserve hot prefixes

2026-03-04: Hedged retries to fallback model variants selected with exponential backoff and jitter; first retry goes to same model with abridged context, second retry routes to quantized micro-model if available
2026-03-06: Instrumentation includes memory_budget_estimate and policy_applied tags for later attribution in cost and quality dashboards
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Spike implemented to estimate per-request memory delta from batch admission window (branch: feat/memory-police/spike). PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1480

2026-03-05: Added policy config schema and runtime flag (POLICE_ENABLED) + unit tests for abridged context trimming logic. CI passing on linux-gpu lanes. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1502

2026-03-07: Integration run on a 50-GPU staging cluster with synthetic workload (long-context chat + short misc). Observed 3x reduction in transient OOMs but tail latency increase on long requests ~18%. Collected traces in dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/runtime/oom-experiments/39502
2026-03-09: Tweaked KV omission ranking to prefer stale segments and preserve last-turn KV; updated hedged retry sequencing to include fast path (0.5s) retry for immediate relief
2026-03-11: Determined threshold tuning and safety clamps; preparing canary rollout plan and runbook (confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/ENG-39502+memory+policing)
risks: Quality regression: abridged context may omit critical information leading to hallucination or incorrect responses
Latency/regret: extra hedged retries could increase overall token cost and P95 latency if misconfigured
Telemetry gaps: incomplete tags could make it hard to attribute degradations to policy versus unrelated regressions
Complexity: introducing per-request memory estimation adds scheduling surface area and potential for admission race conditions
test_plan: Unit: coverage for abridged trimming function, KV selection heuristics, and retry sequencing (target 95% coverage for new modules)
Integration: run synthetic traffic scenarios (50/30/20 mix short/medium/long contexts) with controlled memory headroom to exercise fallbacks
Chaos: force OOM on a single GPU to verify hedged retry routing and safe rollback of in-flight requests
Perf: A/B test measuring cost/token and latency distribution across 1k requests per second on staging cluster
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (staging): feature flag ON for 100% of staging nodes; run 72h synthetic workload and collect metrics
Stage 2 (canary): enable on 5% of prod-serving nodes with read-only traffic mirroring for 48h; monitor p99 OOM, p95 latency, and quality regression metrics
Stage 3 (gradual): 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 6 days with stop-gate thresholds (oom_reduction < 50% or quality_regression_signal > 2x triggers rollback)
Rollback: disable POLICE_ENABLED or set policy.mode=off; run immediate drain and short-circuit hedged retry queue
